acceptance_scope: Independent offline implementation review of the adopted ED-002 synthetic shared-cash contract only. Rejection is limited to the two concrete adapter defects below; it does not reject the adopted modelling contract or reopen existing studies.

blocking_findings.title: Terminal liquidation promotes valuation-only marks into executable prices
blocking_findings.finding: marks_at fills a missing close from a separate valuation-only observation, and state.last_marks loses that distinction. Terminal liquidation then passes the entire last_marks map as both execution prices and NAV marks. A valid mark can therefore generate a terminal MODELLED_FULL_FILL even though the corresponding last-close executable price is absent. This contradicts the adopted separation of valuation marks from execution prices and can label a residual marked holding as liquidated cash.

reproduction.inputs: SYNTHETIC A/B, interval 10, capital 1000, zero costs, lot/quote step 0.01, valid dated permission. Buy A at the second bar open 10. Final bar has open A=10 but no close A; only valuation-only record {ts_ms:30,known_at_ms:30,price:12} supplies its final mark.
reproduction.observed: Primary remains correctly COMPLETE with 100 A and marked NAV 1200. Optional terminal endpoint sells all 100 A at raw_price 12, returns cash 1200/units A=0 and profit_basis=liquidated_cash.
reproduction.expected: The valuation may support marked NAV, but must not supply a terminal executable price. Retain explicitly marked residual units or return an appropriately incomplete terminal endpoint when no permitted last-close execution price exists.
reproduction.impact: Fabricated terminal executability and cost/turnover/realized-versus-unrealized attribution; not a change to the correct primary marked NAV in this counterexample.

blocking_findings.required_closure: Preserve last-close executable-price provenance separately from valuation-only marks and refuse/exclude mark-only terminal fills. Add this missing-close/fresh-mark terminal regression while preserving primary NAV and carry state.

blocking_findings.title: Resumed comparison does not bind its benchmark identities or declared mix
blocking_findings.finding: The carry profile binds symbols/costs/capital/target_contract_id but not btc_symbol, eth_symbol or normalized mix_weights. Those arguments are only syntactically checked on a resumed comparison. Since control callbacks return None once decision_index is nonzero, changed declarations neither refuse nor update the carried control. The returned COMPLETE comparison can silently use a different benchmark instrument/exposure than its current explicit declaration.

reproduction.original: Two-symbol A/B comparison starts with BTC=A, ETH=B, declared mix A=0.25/B=0.25 and a fixed caller contract ID. Carry all four returned states across a contiguous split.
reproduction.changed_identity: Resume with BTC=B and ETH=A under the same ID and financial profile: hold_btc returns COMPLETE while retaining A=100/B=0.
reproduction.changed_mix: Separately resume the original carry with mix_weights={A:0.75}: declared_btc_eth_cash_mix returns COMPLETE while retaining the old A=25/B=25/50%-cash allocation.
reproduction.expected: Reject changed built-in comparison identities or mix declarations on resume, rather than silently returning the old control under the new recipe.
reproduction.impact: Mislabelled benchmark/exposure comparisons and loss of the declared common-contract carry boundary. No new trade is needed for the comparison to become mislabeled.
reproduction.boundary: This is not a request to hash or sandbox an arbitrary candidate callback. The API already documents caller responsibility for that callable. The defect concerns explicit built-in benchmark parameters controlled by simulate_shared_comparison itself.

blocking_findings.required_closure: Bind normalized benchmark instrument identities and declared mix to comparison carry state/profile and validate them before any resumed arm is simulated. Add refusal tests for identity swap and mix change, retaining the existing unchanged-recipe full-versus-split equality.

verified_areas.classification: SHOWN static and focused synthetic regression
verified_areas.detail: One cash/units/basis ledger, exact Fraction settlement, sell-before-buy credits net of costs, lot flooring, quote debit ceil/credit floor, common-factor affordability resizing, proportional basis/dust and exact trade-only NAV/cost reconciliation are implemented. No negative-cash or lot-affordability defect was identified in the reviewed paths.

verified_areas.classification: SHOWN static and focused synthetic regression
verified_areas.detail: Callbacks receive deep copies of completed history; pending targets execute at the one next-open timestamp. Dated permissions are filtered by decision-close knowledge and execution applicability. Missing opens exclude those symbols without target redistribution; valuation-only marks do not fund ordinary executable prices. Frozen holdings remain in NAV/free-capital calculations.

verified_areas.classification: SHOWN static and focused synthetic regression
verified_areas.detail: Batch changes occur on a cloned working state and are returned only after reconciliation. Missing held NAV or required permission invalidates the case; a legitimate prior open fill survives a later missing close, and invalid carry cannot resume as valid performance. Primary pending/cash/basis/history continuity and preceding-close phase anchors have targeted coverage.

verified_areas.classification: SHOWN focused regression, subject to blockers
verified_areas.detail: With unchanged comparison parameters, cash and fixed-unit controls use the same engine/costs and preserve split equality. Optional terminal simulation clones rather than mutates primary state. These positive properties do not close the terminal price-provenance or resumed-control-declaration defects.
